title: Wyckham Insurance claims onramp notes
content:
Call notes + raw capture — Wyckham Insurance (initial onramp)
Attendees: Samira (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood runtime eng), Leah (Redwood CSM),
           Mark Hollis (Wyckham head of claims), Priyanka Rao (Claims ops), Tomas Varela (IT infra)
Date/time: 2025-10-14 11:00am PT (60m)
Tone: exploratory, pragmatic; Wyckham wants a low-risk pilot focused on triage automation for first-notice-of-loss (FNOL).

1) High-level ask / success metrics (what they said)
- Reduce average time to triage FNOL by 40% for property & auto claims (human-in-the-loop).
- Maintain precision on category/classification >= 92% vs current rules engine.
- Latency goal: <200ms median for classification call when routed to hosted variant; for private deployment want p95 < 400ms.
- Throughput: bursts up to 800 req/min during peak business hours for pilot (20 concurrent agents).
- Security: SOC2 + contractual requirements for customer-managed KMS and audit logs for PII access.

2) Data & integration surface
- Sources: phone transcriptions (vendor: SpeakEasy), uploaded claim forms (OCR -> JSON), event metadata from their claims queue (Kafka), and historical claim summaries (S3).
- Integration points wanted: webhook to Redwood hosted API for MVP; later preference for Private VPC deployment so tokens/PHI never leave their VPC.
- Expected payloads: transcription text (up to ~5k chars), OCR structured fields (policy#, dates), and small JSON context (policy tier, prior claims count).

3) Proposed flow (sketch from call)
- Step 1: transcription arrives -> Redwood classify call returns claim type + severity bucket + suggested route (auto, review, fast-track).
- Step 2: if auto-route, Redwood returns extraction hints (entities + confidence) for the claims UI; agent approves/edits and finalizes.
- Step 3: metrics stream to Redwood Console + Wyckham's Datadog. Rollout: canary 2% -> 20% -> full.

4) Nonfunctional constraints & gotchas (their emphasis)
- PHI/PII: cannot allow persistence of full transcriptions in hosted Redwood storage for pilot beyond 30 days unless encrypted with their KMS. They prefer Private for full retention.
- Model interpretability: they want per-decision rationale (top-3 tokens or prompt-window highlights) for audit — note: we can provide token-level saliency approximations but not full explainability guarantees.
- Edge-case docs: scanned PDFs with handwritten notes (bad OCR) are ~18% of intake — high failure mode; will need fallback to human review.
- Policy/regression: they want a QA harness using their labeled set of 12k historical claims to measure precision/recall on nightly runs.
- Throughput spikes correlate with catastrophes (hurricanes) — transient 10x traffic spikes possible; need burst capacity or graceful fallback to simpler model/route.
- Tokenization quirk: noisy transcriptions with timestamps and agent notes cause model hallucinations in extraction; recommend lightweight preprocessing strip timestamps.

5) Deployment preference + security items
- Pilot: start with Redwood Hosted API in a dedicated tenant with strict retention + KMS envelope (bring-your-own-key) and IP allowlist. This reduces time-to-value.
- Target after pilot: Private (VPC) deployment in us-east-1 with private control plane, customer KMS/HSM integration, and exportable audit logs to their SIEM.
- Network: Wyckham uses strict egress rules; they will need peered VPC or VPN; Tomas to share network runbook.

6) Quality evaluation plan (suggestion)
- Use their 12k labeled historical set: split into train/validate/eval (80/10/10). Run nightly evals measuring classification accuracy, entity extraction F1, and false-positive critical errors.
- Setup prompt/eval regression alerts: if classification accuracy drops >2% vs baseline for 3 consecutive runs, auto-roll back to previous model version.

7) Cost sensitivity / model choice notes
- They asked about cheaper quantized models for bulk extraction vs higher-quality chat models for judgment tasks. Recommend hybrid: distilled/quantized for extraction/classification path, larger model behind ‘review assist’ route.
- Billing: they will centralize on committed reserved capacity after pilot if SLA and latency hold — mention Redwood Dedicated pricing in the follow-up.

8) Action items (who/what/when)
- Tomas (Wyckham) -> provide network runbook + firewall egress rules by 2025-10-21. (task created: JIRA-CLM-1187)
- Samira -> prototype a classification prompt + 10-shot examples and push to sandbox (demo) by 2025-10-22.
- Diego -> validate throughput on dedicated GPU profile (A10-like sim) and simulate 1k rpm burst; share perf numbers by 2025-10-24.
- Leah -> draft SOW outline and pilot success criteria; attach legal checklist for KMS/BYOK by 2025-10-27.
- Wyckham (Priyanka) -> export 2 months of anonymized historical FNOL for initial eval set by 2025-10-28.

9) Open questions / risk register (capture for follow-up)
- How do we prove non-persistence for edge cases where we need short-term caching for batching? (Samira/Diego to propose cached TTL/ephemeral mode.)
- What’s the minimum audit log retention Wyckham legal will accept if hosted solution used? (Leah to escalate to legal.)
- If OCR quality stays poor for 18% of forms, do they want to invest in collection of better scans or improve model tolerance? Cost tradeoffs to quantify.

10) Quick prompt example (working)
- Goal: classify claim from transcript + return {claim_type, severity, suggested_route, evidence_spans}
- Instruction (sketch): "Read the transcript. Output only JSON with fields: claim_type (one of: auto, property, liability, other), severity (low/medium/high), suggested_route (auto/review/escalate), evidence_spans: list of short text snippets that justify the decision."
- Note: include a 5-shot example covering ambiguous agent comments to reduce hallucination.

11) Misc notes / conversation fragments (raw)
- Mark: "We want the agent to be faster, not replaced — give our triage team decision confidence."
- Priyanka: worried about model drift after policy changes in the industry (fraud patterns). Wants monthly retrain/eval cadence.
- Tomas: "We have a strict SOC2 matrix; we also need HSM-based key access that our security team can audit."

Summary: Pilot looks viable as hosted-first (BYOK + retention controls) to speed delivery. Key blockers: network runbook, anonymized historical dataset, and performance validation for bursts. Next sync after tasks completed: 2025-10-29 (proposed 30m).

-- end of scratchpad --

(Internal notes: keep this in users/ so SEs can iterate. Should convert to a neat onboarding playbook in shared_drives/engineering/solutions-engineering after pilot sign-off.)
